chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Faḍālah, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the muleteers who travel back and forth, and he said: When they press on seriously in travel, then they should shorten.

The proper way of understanding these two reports is what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Kulaynī, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned. He said: This is to be understood as referring to one who treats the two stopping places as one stopping place, so he shortens on the road and performs in full at the stopping place. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned...

key_terms.السَّيْرَ: traveling or moving along the route
key_terms.الْمَنْزِلَيْنِ: the two stopping places or lodging points
key_terms.الْمُكَارِينَ: transport workers or muleteers who travel repeatedly for hire
key_terms.جَدُّوا: they pressed on seriously and earnestly
key_terms.فَلْيَقْصُرُوا: then they should shorten the salat (prayer)
key_terms.وَيُتِمُّ: he performs the salat (prayer) in full
key_terms.يَخْتَلِفُونَ: go back and forth repeatedly in travel

ai.seo_question: When must frequently traveling workers shorten their salat (prayer) during travel?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of salat (prayer) for transport workers who travel repeatedly. It indicates that when such travelers undertake serious movement on the road, they shorten their salat (prayer), while a scholarly clarification explains the distinction between shortening during transit and completing the salat (prayer) at the place of stay.
